title: GKE Autopilot Pod Scaling

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.3.26 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.3.26 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:pubsub:message` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" resource.type="k8s_cluster" ("FailedScheduling" OR "Insufficient cpu" OR "Insufficient memory")
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.26_gke_autopilot_pod_scalin_26"
| sort -_time
description: Autopilot scales node pools automatically; failed scale-outs leave pods pending and degrade SLOs.
value: Detecting gke autopilot pod scaling early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable GKE logging and filter for scheduling events. Correlate with pending pod metrics if exported. Alert on rising pending pod count or repeated scale failures.
visualization: Timeline (scheduling failures), Table (cluster, reason, count), Line chart (pending pods).
knownFalsePositives: During a roll-out, nodes come and go and metrics briefly look off. We ignore short windows that line up with a deployment and we focus on steady-state failures after the cluster is calm again.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable GKE logging and filter for scheduling events. Correlate with pending pod metrics if exported. Alert on rising pending pod count or repeated scale failures.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" resource.type="k8s_cluster" ("FailedScheduling" OR "Insufficient cpu" OR "Insufficient memory")
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.26_gke_autopilot_pod_scalin_26"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect gke autopilot pod scaling. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_26_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Timeline (scheduling failures), Table (cluster, reason, count), Line chart (pending pods)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of gke autopilot pod scaling so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
